summary_markdown:
The current seed generation process is unstable, failing on the server during authorization. Security concerns were raised regarding the use of integer IDs for seeds, suggesting a token-based ID system to prevent unauthorized access and hacking.

Regarding implementation, it was discussed that relying on existing functionality (like `/api/seed/NN`) is problematic because it performs multiple dangerous actions beyond just returning data. A new build or significant refactoring is recommended over patching the current system.

For campaign integration, while full UI-only operation might lose necessary seed logic, a client-side authorization flow was suggested where the user logs in to implicitly pass the user context to the server.

Finally, efforts will be made to remove the reliance on integer IDs for seeds and potentially use string-generated IDs. The instability of the seed process itself (causing Nest processes to crash) must also be addressed.
decisions: Seed ID generation should switch from integers to a token-based system.
The current seed API endpoint is deemed unsafe and requires replacement or major refactoring.
A client-side login/registration flow will handle user context for campaign integration.
action_items: Refactor the unstable seed generation process to prevent server crashes.
